name: Ashveil Acidpulse Rave Harness Set
description: A Tier 1 underground rave rig built from salvaged industrial webbing and reclaimed synth-mesh, dyed in layers of acid-washed teal and burnt copper that glow faintly under UV. The core piece is a wide-strap chest harness of braided cargo strapping over a sheer bioluminescent underlayer — a secondhand strip of reactive Lumiflex fabric, originally military-grade, now flickering erratically to ambient bass frequencies in pulses of pale green and amber. Paired with asymmetric shorts cut from patched reclaimed neoprene, one leg fully exposed to show off chrome or scarred skin, the other wrapped in a torn fishnet stocking fused with conductive thread that sparks micro-flashes at the knee. Footwear is battered platform boots — salvaged Kelvex transit safety soles with the reflective strips left on — rising to mid-shin and laced with fiber-optic cord that traces the pulse of the wearer's BCI heartbeat readout in stuttering white light.
functionality: Harness has hidden interior pockets sized for stims, a flat-fold emergency breather patch, and a small EMP-shielded pouch for BCI hardware. Boot soles retain original slip-resistance and acid-rain rated outer coating. Conductive thread in the fishnet acts as a basic proximity sensor — wearer feels a faint buzz when someone moves too close in crowd.
what_it_says: This is someone who builds their own identity from the city's cast-offs and wears it like armor. Not trying to look expensive — trying to look alive. The erratic Lumiflex pulse says the tech is secondhand and doesn't care. The exposed chrome or scars say neither does the wearer.
worn_by: chrome-arm scrappers on their one night off
bioluminescent geneware users who don't bother covering up
manufacturer: Self-assembled — components from Ashveil Salvage Markets and grey-market Lumiflex strip vendors
story_hooks: The EMP-shielded pouch contains something that isn't BCI hardware — a stolen data chip that three different factions are currently hunting through the rave.
The Lumiflex strip's erratic pulse is not a malfunction — it's syncing to a broadcast frequency that only this wearer can detect, and the pattern is a message.
A Tier 4 fashion scout photographs the wearer from across the rave floor and offers an obscene amount of QUANTA for the harness on the spot — someone powerful wants it, and not for the fashion.
